steps.observation: Work on this for 30 seconds; do not stop early. Name three causes of World War I.

steps.action:
Here are three major, commonly cited causes of World War I:

1. Militarism and the arms race  
   • In the decades before 1914, the great powers of Europe—especially Germany, Britain, France, and Russia—dramatically expanded and modernized their armies and navies.  
   • This buildup fostered a climate in which leaders and publics alike regarded war not only as possible but, in some circles, as inevitable or even desirable for resolving diplomatic tensions.

2. Entangling alliances  
   • Two main alliance blocs solidified: the Triple Alliance (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Italy) and the Triple Entente (France, Russia, Britain).  
   • Leaders believed these alliances would deter aggression, but instead they created a domino effect: once Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia, the network of obligations rapidly pulled the other powers into the conflict.

3. Nationalism and imperial rivalries  
   • Intense national pride and competition for colonies heightened tensions—especially in the Balkans, where Slavic nationalism challenged Austria-Hungary, and in Africa and Asia, where European empires vied for territory.  
   • This atmosphere made diplomatic compromises harder and turned local crises, such as the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in June 1914, into a broader continental—and eventually global—war.
